newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Britain's Queen of Hearts visits Sydney.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Queen of Hearts visits Sydney.

text.p: Sydney's social elite turned up in force on Thursday to dine and dance with Britain's Princess Diana at a fund-raising dinner for a cardiac research institute.
The princess is no longer a royal since her divorce two months ago, but she got red-carpet treatment at Thursday's dinner -- and a serenade from British rock star Sting.
More than 800 guests paid A$1,000 ($790) each to attend the dinner, to fund the Victor Chang Cardiac Research Institute, named after a Sydney heart surgeon murdered in 1991.
Wearing an off-the-shoulder electric-blue gown, the princess danced first with former New South Wales state premier Neville Wran, an avowed republican who heads the institute.
On Friday, she was due to visit the institute and a hospital before a charity lunch for homeless children. She was to visit a city hospice on Saturday and to leave Sydney on Sunday.
Princess Diana last visited Sydney eight years ago with her former husband Prince Charles.
